Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

description in advance", "output": "I need you to make a working copy of the west stairwell rehearsal recording and place it in location A104 before the listening session on Thursday at six thirty in the evening. The source file is the April twelfth recording with the full company and the warm-up before the first scene. Please keep the original file where it is and do not rename it while you are making the copy. The folder label should say “west stairwell april twelve working copy” so people can tell it apart from the unedited source. Bram is helping me check the sound on this one, and he has already marked the section where the door latch rattles, so leave his notes attached to the copy.

The archive has several versions of the same rehearsal because the cast tried two different entrances that night. The one I mean begins with Mara asking everyone to move the chairs away from the blue tape, and then the piano starts before anyone speaks. There is a short cough in the left channel at about four minutes, but that is part of the recording and should stay in place. The later version begins with the cast coming in from the lobby, so please do not use that file even though the title is almost the same. The date in the file name is April twelve, not April thirteen, and the duration is just under fifty minutes. Bram’s notes refer to the earlier entrance and not the lobby version, so the distinction matters for the review.

1. Copy details. First, use the file with the name “west stairwell april twelve full company and warm up.” If the archive search shows two copies, compare the opening thirty seconds before choosing the source. Second, put the new copy inside the current season folder and keep it beside the rehearsal notes rather than in the public listening folder. Third, retain the original recording date and add “working copy” at the end of the copy name. Do not replace “full company” with “cast,” because the label is used by the sound team for searching. Fourth, include Bram’s sound notes as an attachment and keep the time stamps in the notes exactly as he wrote them. The notes mention the latch at twenty-one minutes and forty seconds and the piano pedal at thirty-six minutes and ten seconds.

When you check the file, please listen to the opening and the final minute rather than playing the whole recording. The opening should contain Mara’s chair instruction and the first piano cue. The last minute should include the cast waiting for the stage manager to call the end of the take. There is a little handling noise after that, but it belongs to the same file. Do not trim either end or apply noise reduction to the copy. The archive playback sometimes makes the left channel sound quieter than the right, so compare the two channels using headphones before you decide whether something is missing. If the playback equipment changes the balance, just leave a note for the review and do not edit the sound.

I also need the folder to remain useful to people who were not at that rehearsal. Please keep the existing description with the recording and add one sentence saying that the chairs were moved before the first scene and that the piano began before the dialogue. Do not write that the cast completed the scene, because the recording stops during the rehearsal and we do not have a separate note confirming what happened afterward. Use the date as it appears in the source record, and do not turn the description into a review of the performance. The copy is for listening and comparison, not for deciding which entrance was better.

There is a small paper sign-out sheet in the blue binder at the archive desk, and it has the rehearsal date and the initials of the person who brought the recorder back. Please leave that sheet in the binder rather than scanning it into the recording folder. It includes other people’s names from the same week and is not part of the audio record. If you need to mention the sign-out information in the folder description, use only the date and do not copy the initials. The recorder itself was returned on Friday morning according to the binder, so there is no need to add a return time from memory.

For the review folder, make a separate note that the microphone was placed near the downstage door and that the piano was on the right side of the room. Those details may help the listening group understand why the latch is clearer on the left channel. Do not state that the microphone caused the rattle, and do not label the sound as a fault. We only know what can be heard on this recording. The room diagram from that evening is filed with the stage manager’s papers and is not needed for this copy. If the group asks for it later, we can look for it then.

When the copy is ready for the listening session, keep it restricted to the rehearsal archive team because two voices in the warm-up belong to visiting students who did not sign the public release form. The existing access setting for the source should remain unchanged, and this request is only about the new working copy. Do not send a link to the full company or put it on the public page. The listening session is internal, and Bram will be there to explain his sound notes, but he is not approving the recording on behalf of the archive.

Finally, please leave the copy name and folder description visible in the file list so the session lead can find them without opening every version. If there is already a working copy from a later rehearsal, do not overwrite it, because that recording has a different piano cue and is being used for another review. Keep the two dates separate and put the April twelve copy next to its own rehearsal notes. The session lead asked to begin with this recording and then compare it with the later entrance version once both files are open. The final comparison will happen during the session and should not be written into the folder description in advance."}]
